Use this reusable template to write and share your knit sock patterns in Markdown. Fill in the bracketed sections with your pattern details. This template works for cuff-down constructions.

### Gauge

[e.g., 32 sts x 40 rounds / 4 in / 10 cm in stockinette or main stitch pattern]

Swatch in the round, not flat, to get accurate sock gauge. If using stranded colorwork, swatch in the colorwork pattern — aim for matching colorwork and stockinette gauge. Adjust needle sizes as needed. Wash and block your swatch before measuring.

### Heel

```plaintext
[Instructions for heel flap, turn, and gusset, or short-row heel]
```

For a reinforced heel, use a slipped stitch pattern (\*SL1, k1\* on right side, \*SL1, p1\* on wrong side). You can also hold a second nylon thread together with your yarn for extra durability at the heel.

**Heel flap + turn + gusset (W&T method):**

```plaintext
Heel is worked flat over the second half of stitches (after MR marker).

Row 1 (RS): Sl1, k to end.
Row 2 (WS): Sl1, p to end.
Repeat Rows 1-2 for [N] rows total.

Heel Turn:
Row 1 (RS): Sl1, k until [N] sts remain, W&T.
Row 2 (WS): Sl1, p until [N] sts remain, W&T.
Row 3: K until 1 st before wrapped st, W&T.
Row 4: P until 1 st before wrapped st, W&T.
Repeat Rows 3-4 until [N] wrapped sts on each side.
Final Row (RS): K to wrapped st, k wrap together with st.
Final Row (WS): P to wrapped st, p wrap together with st.

Gusset:
Pick up and knit [N] sts along heel flap edge. Place BOR marker.
Knit across instep sts. Pick up and knit [N] sts along other heel flap edge.
Decrease Rnd: K to [N] sts before MR marker, ssk, sm, k to [N] sts before BOR marker, k2tog.
Knit 1 rnd even.
Repeat until [N] sts remain.
```

### Foot

```plaintext
[Knit all rounds until sock measures [N] in / cm shorter than desired total length. For a good fit, knit 0.5-0.75 in / 1-2 cm shorter than actual foot length — negative ease ensures a snug fit.]
```

**Colorwork band (optional):** Work [N] rounds from a colorwork chart on the foot for a decorative accent.

### Toe

```plaintext
[Instructions for toe decreases and grafting or closing]
```

Use Kitchener stitch (grafting) for an invisible seamless toe. Pulling the yarn through the final stitches creates a pointier toe that may not fit as well in shoes.
